content.overview: Section 225 provides that the expenses of and incidental to an investigation by an inspector appointed by the Central Government under this Chapter shall be defrayed in the first instance by the Central Government, but the following persons shall, to the extent mentioned, be liable to repay the Central Government: (a) any person who is convicted on a prosecution instituted as a result of the investigation, or who is ordered to pay damages or restore property in proceedings brought under section 224, may be ordered to repay the whole or part; (b) any company in whose name proceedings are brought under section 224 shall be liable to repay, unless the Central Government otherwise directs; and (c) where the investigation was in pursuance of an order under section 213 on an application of members, the applicants shall be liable, subject to the limit of any security given under section 214. Any amount for which a company is liable is a first charge on the property of the company.
content.glance: CG defrays investigation expenses first; recoverable from convicted persons / those ordered to pay damages / company in recovery proceedings / member-applicants (subject to s. 214 security); company liability is a first charge on its property.
content.study: The expenses of and incidental to an investigation by an inspector appointed by the Central Government under this Chapter shall be defrayed in the first instance by the Central Government, but the following persons shall, to the extent mentioned in this section, be liable to repay the Central Government. Current-law framing: identify that CG bears expenses first; map recovery paths — convicted person, person ordered to pay damages or restore property under s. 224, company in whose name recovery is brought, and member-applicants under s. 213 subject to s. 214 security; note first charge on company property where the company is liable.

sections.heading: Primary Bearer
sections.body: Expenses of and incidental to the investigation are defrayed in the first instance by the Central Government.

sections.heading: Recovery Paths
sections.body: Recoverable from: (a) convicted persons or persons ordered to pay damages/restore property under s. 224; (b) the company where proceedings are brought in its name under s. 224 (unless CG otherwise directs); (c) member-applicants under s. 213, subject to s. 214 security.

sections.heading: Charge
sections.body: Any amount for which a company is liable under this section is a first charge on the property of the company.

examples.title: Recovery from convicted person
examples.body: After a s. 224 prosecution based on an inspector’s report, a director is convicted. Under s. 225 the court may order him to repay the whole or part of the investigation expenses to the Central Government.

examples.title: Member-applicant security
examples.body: Investigation was ordered on a members’ application under s. 213 and security was taken under s. 214. Under s. 225 those applicants are liable to the extent of that security for investigation expenses.

hypotheticals.question: Does the company always bear the full cost of every investigation under Chapter XIV?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. The Central Government defrays expenses in the first instance. The company becomes liable in the paths the section identifies (e.g. where recovery proceedings are brought in its name under s. 224), and that liability is a first charge on its property. Other paths recover from convicted persons or member-applicants.

distinctions.title: Expenses of investigation (s. 225) vs security for costs (s. 214)
distinctions.left: Who ultimately bears/recovers investigation expenses after the event
distinctions.right: Security that may be required from member-applicants before inspector appointment

misconceptions.trap: The Central Government always absorbs investigation costs with no recovery.
misconceptions.correction: Section 225 provides structured recovery from convicted persons, persons ordered to pay damages, the company in recovery proceedings, and member-applicants subject to s. 214 security.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 225 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm CG bore expenses first. II. Map recovery path (convict / damages / company / applicants). III. Note first charge if company liable. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Expense facts; recovery path; charge if applicable; precise relief.

examTips: Recovery from convicts, damages order, company, member-applicants.
